items: <!-- Since there are \(n\) pure strategies, the first piece of information is a distribution \(\bar p = \langle p_1,\dots, p_n\rangle\), where \(0 \leq p_i \leq 1\) and \(\sum p_i = 1\), where each \(p_i\) indicates the proportion of the population that follows strategy \(S_i\). The second piece of information is a vector \(\bar W(\bar p) = \langle W_1(\bar p), \dots, W_n(\bar p)\rangle\), where \(W_i(\bar p)\) denotes the expected payoff of \(S_i\) in the current state of the population. -->
